correctness.rationale: Automorphisms of K_m square K_n are independent row/column permutations, augmented by global swap iff m=n; this includes K_2 square K_2. Unique landmarks pointwise fix their occupied rows and columns. For m!=n, marked-neighbor common counts n-2 vs m-2 distinguish which coordinate matches a landmark in round two. For square nonattacking F, first-round adjacency labels unordered coordinate-category pairs and swap realizes exactly their orbits. For square attacking F, two marked squares determine a first-round-definable shared row; intersecting it with each off-row marked neighborhood yields first-round singleton crosspoints, which let round two distinguish columns and then rows. Thus the class counts AB or binomial(A+1,2) and sizes follow. Explicit nonsquare single-marker and square 4x4 three-marker configurations establish 2-round sharpness. An independent direct orbit/refinement implementation tested 891 finite marked patterns, including the sharp 4x4 example.
residual_risks: m,n>=2; unique colours assigned individually to members of F only.
No claim for arbitrary initial partitions or 3+ Cartesian factors.
Finite enumeration not an all-board proof.
